newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai August inflation rise disappoints market.
newsitem.headline: Thai August inflation rise disappoints market.

text.p: Soaring food prices helped drive Thai inflation to 5.5 percent year-on-year in August but financial markets considered the result only mildly disappointing, analysts said on Tuesday.

The rise was marginally above the 5.4 percent year-on-year increase posted in July. But it was the first increase in the monthly figures after five consecutive declines in inflation growth, according to Monday's official commerce ministry data.

"The August figure was only mildly disappointing. We had expected it to be flat. We see a lower trend in year-on-year monthly inflation growth for the rest of the year," said James Marshall, head of research at Capital Nomura Securities.
He told Reuters the easier inflation picture ahead for Thailand could be pegged to a noticeable slowdown in the national economy.
He projected Thailand's gross domestic product growth in 1996 would dip below 7.0 percent from 8.6 percent in 1995.

Some other analysts and stockbrokers saw the August figure as another negative economic indicator after the central bank said last week Thai exports rose only 3.8 percent in January-July against 26.2 percent the same period a year ago.

Thai stocks dipped early, with the benchmark SET Index off 6.14 points at 1,080.09 at midday. Some brokers said investors were disappointed at the August figure which they had believed would remain flat or even decline from the previous month.

The commerce ministry said the August food and beverage index, carrying a relatively heavy 39.3 percent weighting in the overall consumer price index (CPI), rose a hefty 9.1 percent year-on-year and 2.3 percent over July,
The increase largely reflected higher seasonal demand during the annual All Souls Day observed by a large ethnic Chinese community in Thailand.
It said vegetables and fruit prices shot up 11.0 percent in August from July, and meat and poultry rose 2.2 percent.

"With the big August jump, I don't think the government's inflation target of 5.5 percent this year is achievable. We are raising our 1996 projection to 5.7-5.8 percent," said Chatchai Saelee of Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.
"The only non-inflationary hope that we have now is for Thailand to be spared later this year from extensive flooding that we saw in late 1995," he said.
Central bank economist Bandid Nijathaworn said late on Monday he was relatively surprised by the August price hike after the index's steady slower growth in recent months.
He declined to say whether overall 1996 inflation could be restrained to 5.5 percent, a target adjusted up by the central bank in late July from its earlier projection of 4.9 percent for this year.
Consumers are increasingly frustrated by the rising food prices.

According to a survey by a Thai university last week of 114 fresh food markets in Bangkok, 35.6 percent of 711 shoppers interviewed said they could not bear what they called soaring food prices in the past three months.
The survey showed that pork cost about 80-90 baht (US$3.20-$3.60) per kg last week, up from 60 baht in June.
